title: Atomic attention kernel sampling labnotes
content:
Purpose
------
Quick working notebook capturing microbenchmarks, anomalous edge cases, and sampling methodology for attention kernels. Goal: produce reliable signals to decide dynamic kernel-selection thresholds (flash vs paged vs fused) and identify short-burst tail-latency causes seen in production.

Executive summary (working)
-------------------------
- Observed reproducible 95th/99th tail spikes on small-batch, medium-sequence (batch 1-4, seq 256-1024) workloads.
- FlashAttention microbench is fastest median for long sequences but shows high variance when concurrent small kernels coalesce at scheduler boundary.
- Paged-attention paths reduce memory pressure for >1k seqs but have higher per-token overhead for short prefixes.
- A fused-ops variant we built reduces kernel count but at some sequence shapes it triggers shared-memory spills, increasing latency ~1.6x (seen on A100 80GB, driver CUDA 12.2).

Environment / reproducibility notes
---------------------------------
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (driver 535.XX), test H100 cluster for cross-checks (driver 555.XX).
- CUDA: 12.2 / cuDNN 9.4 / pytorch-nightly + custom runtime.
- Profilers: Nsight Systems (nsys 2024.*), CUPTI sampling, nvprof archival traces for older runs.
- Test harness: bench_attn.py (local script) that runs synthetic, KV-cache warm/cold, and mixed-length traces. Seeded RNG for batching order.
- NVTX ranges: bench_attn wraps each micro-inference in NVTX push/pop with kernel labels (flash/paged/fused).

Commands used (examples)
-----------------------
- nsys timeline: nsys profile -o /tmp/nsys_run --trace=cuda,cublas,nvtx python -u bench_attn.py --model gpt-2 --seq 512 --batch 1 --iters 200
- quick microbench: python bench_attn.py --kernel flash_v2 --batch 1 --seq 512 --warm 20 --iters 400
- smreport (for occupancy analysis): ./smreport.py /tmp/nsys_run.qdrep --kernels 'flash'

Microbench matrix (representative)
----------------------------------
- Sequences: 16, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 16, 32
- KV state: cold (first token), warm (after prefix length 128), long-cache (shared KV across calls)
- Kernels: flash_v2, paged_attn_v1, fused_attn_splitkv, fused_attn_inplace
- Metrics: median latency (ms), p95 (ms), p99 (ms), tokens/s, GPU utilization (SM), L2 read/write (GB/s), shared mem spills count (approx)

Representative results (flattened numbers; see linked traces for raw TSV)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
- batch=1, seq=512: flash_v2: median 63ms, p95 120ms, p99 220ms; paged_v1: median 85ms, p95 98ms, p99 125ms; fused_inplace: median 71ms, p95 160ms (spikes)
- batch=4, seq=128: flash_v2: median 32ms, p95 48ms, p99 95ms; paged_v1: median 42ms, p95 58ms; fused_splitkv: median 36ms, p95 40ms
- batch=1, seq=2048: flash_v2: median 380ms, p95 420ms, p99 470ms; paged_v1: median 410ms, p95 430ms
- observed: fused_inplace regresses specifically on seq ranges 256-1024 when model dim=4096 due to shared-memory spilling into global memory (verified via CUPTI counters).

Observations and hypotheses (raw)
--------------------------------
1) Kernel launch serialization + small kernel overhead: When we coalesce multiple tiny attention kernels from separate requests (PLB-like arrival), kernel launch latency dominates -> p99 increases.
   - hypothesis: CUDA stream scheduling and driver-side batching cause serialization.
   - quick check: enable CUDA_MPS or use fewer streams; p99 reduces ~30% locally.
2) Fusion spill cases: Fused kernels that attempt to reduce kernel count end up using more shared memory; on some shapes this exceeds per-block shared memory and performance collapses as memory spills occur.
   - evidence: CUPTI spilled_local_memory counter + sudden increase in global mem traffic.
3) Paged attention variance: Paged path has higher deterministic overheads but better stability for very long sequences (>1500) due to reduced working set and fewer L2 thrashes.
4) FlashAttention variance source: Flash kernels use aggressive tiling and warp-level reductions; sensitivity to sequence remainder and padding pattern leads to warp divergence in some microcases.

Dirty notes / scratch ideas
--------------------------
- We should instrument kernel entry/exit with finer NVTX (per-block) in debug builds to see distribution of block runtimes for problem shapes.
- Try hybrid-engine: for batch=1 seq in [128,1024] prefer paged when measured L2 miss rate > X. Need cheap runtime heuristic.
- Consider a lightweight preflight: sample first token(s) latency for different kernels with short-circuit comparator (2x attempts) and pick policy at request start. Not ideal for per-token streaming but workable for single-shot generation.

Planned experiments (short list)
-------------------------------
- EXP-A: Turn off kernel fusion for dim=4096 models and run full sweep (batches 1/4/16, seq=64..2048) to measure deltas. Owner: Priya. Target: reproduce in CI. (JIRA SRV-5142)
- EXP-B: Add an occupancy-aware fallback: if free shared memory< threshold for shape, do not use fused_inplace. Implement as heuristic in kernel selector. Owner: Liam.
- EXP-C: MPS vs single-process: run 20 workload mixes to see cross-talk effect of stream scheduling on tail latency. Owner: Ethan.
- EXP-D: Add an on-demand micro-sample switch: measure 4 warm tokens across flash/paged and choose for remainder of request. Latency cost vs gain tradeoff. Owner: Sofia.

Data collection checklist (what to commit to storage)
----------------------------------------------------
- For each run: include nsight(.qdrep or .nsys), summary CSV (shape,batch,kernel,median,p95,p99,tokens/s,sm_util,L2 bw), CUPTI metrics snapshot.
- Keep raw traces for 7 days in /mnt/attn-traces/ for debugging. Only push to S3 on regressions.

Immediate action items (next 72h)
---------------------------------
- [ ] Priya: run EXP-A, push CSVs + traces to /mnt/attn-traces/exp-a/ (deadline: 2026-03-08)
- [ ] Liam: prototype a shared-memory check in kernel selector (PR draft) and add unit tests for shapes that spilled (deadline: 2026-03-11)
- [ ] Ethan: instrument bench to emit NVTX id-to-kernel-name mapping and add a debug flag to produce block-level timing histograms (deadline: 2026-03-07)
- [ ] Sofia: run MPS tests and mixed-traffic profiles; capture p99 deltas (deadline: 2026-03-09)

Questions / open items
----------------------
- How aggressively should the runtime switch kernels? Cost of preflight measurement vs wasted cycles if wrong.
- Can we get per-block shared-memory usage stat cheaply from kernel metadata instead of running a dynamic check?
- Is CUDA MPS available for dedicated capacity instances in Dedicated offering? If not, relevance to hosted production is limited.

Appendix: quick debug outputs (snippets)
--------------------------------------
- CUPTI: spilled_local_memory: 482 (high) for fused_inplace on seq=512, batch=1
- nsys snippet: [CUDA memcpy HtoD] 0.12ms, [flash_attn_kernel] 62.8ms, [fused_inplace_kern] 70.9ms, [spill memcpy] 9.3ms
- sm report: occupancy 0.78, active warps 52%, average block-local shared mem 48KB/64KB (hit threshold)

Notes-to-self (informal)
-----------------------
- don't forget to check an older driver (535 vs 555) — behavior changed once in Nov 2024 with new L2 caching heuristics.
- Consider reaching out to upstream FlashAttention author to discuss remainder/padding handling (might be known).

End of labnotes
--------------
These are intentionally informal. The goal is to converge on a reproducible decision matrix for runtime kernel selection that minimizes p99 across common production shapes while preserving median throughput. Keep iterating and push concrete CSVs + traces to the linked JIRA ticket.
